interactionPlan.concept: In DAG backpropagation, a forward branch (copying a value) becomes a backward summation of gradients, while a forward merge becomes a backward split of gradients.
elements: Nodes: 8 rectangular yellow-orange computation blocks
Forward paths: Directed curved arrows showing bottom-to-top activation flow
Backward paths: Overlay arrows showing top-to-bottom gradient flow
Branch point: Node at the bottom-right branching into two parallel paths
Merge point: Nodes at the top-left merging into a single top block
Labels: Activation values (forward) and gradient values (backward) overlaying nodes and edges
Formulas: Mathematical representation of branch and merge operations shown near nodes

interactions.label: Propagation Mode
interactions.teaches: how the direction of flow and the operations at branch/merge points invert during backpropagation
the mathematical derivative and local Jacobian operation of each specific node

demo_steps.title: The Forward Pass
demo_steps.narration: Activations flow upwards through the DAG. At the bottom-right, a single value branches (copies) into two paths. Near the top, two paths merge (concatenate) to feed into the final layer.

demo_steps.title: The Backward Pass
demo_steps.narration: Gradients flow downwards from the loss at the top. The directions of all arrows are reversed as we compute derivatives using the chain rule.

demo_steps.title: Branching Becomes Summation
demo_steps.narration: Look at the bottom-right node: during the forward pass, it branched one signal to two paths. During the backward pass, the gradients flowing back from both paths summate here.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Because a branched variable influences the loss through multiple distinct pathways, its total gradient is the sum of the gradients flowing back from all of those pathways.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the 8-block DAG layout with a warm yellow/cream fill (#FCE3B4) and dark borders. Use smooth, curved Bezier arrows to connect the blocks exactly as in the reference. In 'Forward Pass' mode, highlight arrows in blue flowing upwards with small sample values. In 'Backward Pass' mode, highlight arrows in red/pink flowing downwards, showcasing gradient summation (e.g., 2.0 + 3.0 = 5.0) at the bottom-right branch node.
